result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [integrations.otel.OTelExporter]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | Pointblank description: Export Pointblank validation results as OpenTelemetry signals. twitter-card: title: >- [integrations.otel.OTelExporter]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | Pointblank description: Export Pointblank validation results as OpenTelemetry signals. title: >- [integrations.otel.OTelExporter]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Export Pointblank validation results as OpenTelemetry signals. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Export Pointblank validation results as OpenTelemetry signals. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/integrations/otel.py#L30-L695){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature integrations.otel.OTelExporter( *, meter_name="pointblank", meter_version=None, enable_metrics=True, enable_tracing=False, enable_logging=False, meter_provider=None, tracer_provider=None, logger_provider=None, metric_prefix="pb.validation", log_level="warning", extra_attributes=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} OpenTelemetry (OTel) is a vendor-neutral standard for application telemetry, which backends such as Grafana, Datadog, New Relic and Prometheus can receive. An `OTelExporter` sends the results of an interrogated [`Validate`](`pointblank.Validate`) object to OTel, so that data quality shows up in the same dashboards and alerts as the rest of a pipeline's telemetry. Call [`export()`](`pointblank.integrations.otel.OTelExporter.export`) after [`interrogate()`](`pointblank.Validate.interrogate`) to send the results. For an export that happens at the end of every interrogation, use [`emit_otel()`](`pointblank.emit_otel`) in [`FinalActions`](`pointblank.FinalActions`) instead (it sends metrics only). An export can produce three kinds of signal: - **Metrics** (on by default). There are counters of the steps (`{prefix}.steps.total`, `{prefix}.steps.passed` and `{prefix}.steps.failed`), of the test units (`{prefix}.test_units.total`, `{prefix}.test_units.passed` and `{prefix}.test_units.failed`) and of the steps that exceeded each threshold level (`{prefix}.threshold.warning`, `{prefix}.threshold.error` and `{prefix}.threshold.critical`). There are gauges of the overall pass rate (`{prefix}.pass_rate`) and of the interrogation time in seconds (`{prefix}.duration`), and a histogram of the step processing times (`{prefix}.step.duration`). Here `{prefix}` is the `metric_prefix=` value. Counters add up over exports, while a gauge keeps the latest value. - **Traces** (`enable_tracing=True`). A `pb.validate` span covers the interrogation, with a `pb.validate.step` child span for each step. A step's span has its test unit counts and fractions and the threshold levels it exceeded. The `pb.validate` span also has a `threshold_breach` event for each threshold level that each step exceeded. - **Logs** (`enable_logging=True`). There is one log record for each step that exceeded a threshold, at the highest level it exceeded (`WARNING`, `ERROR` or `CRITICAL`). The `log_level=` value sets the lowest level that is logged. Every signal has the attributes `pb.tbl_name`, `pb.label`, `pb.owner` and `pb.version` (for the ones that are set in the `Validate` object), plus those in `extra_attributes=`. The signals for individual steps also have `pb.step.i`, `pb.step.assertion_type` and `pb.step.column`. The signals go to the providers given as `meter_provider=`, `tracer_provider=` and `logger_provider=`. Without them, metrics and traces go to OTel's global providers, which discard everything until the application sets up the OTel SDK (for example, with an OTLP exporter that sends to a collector). Log records have no global provider to fall back on, so logging needs `logger_provider=`. The OTel packages are an optional dependency, installed with `pip install pointblank[otel]`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [meter_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["pointblank"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The name that identifies Pointblank as the source of the signals (the OTel instrumentation scope), used for the meter, the tracer and the logger. The default is `"pointblank"`. [meter_version]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The version of the instrumentation scope. The default is `None`, which uses the installed version of Pointblank. [enable_metrics]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to send the metrics. The default is `True`. [enable_tracing]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to send the trace spans. The default is `False`. [enable_logging]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to send log records for the steps that exceeded a threshold. This needs `logger_provider=`. The default is `False`. [meter_provider]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [MeterProvider | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An OTel `MeterProvider` for the metrics. The default is `None`, which uses the global meter provider. [tracer_provider]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [TracerProvider | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An OTel `TracerProvider` for the trace spans. The default is `None`, which uses the global tracer provider. [logger_provider]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An OTel `LoggerProvider` for the log records, needed when `enable_logging=True`. The default is `None`. [metric_prefix]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["pb.validation"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The prefix for the names of the metrics. The default is `"pb.validation"`. [log_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["warning"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The lowest threshold level that produces a log record: `"warning"` (every step that exceeded a threshold), `"error"` or `"critical"`. The default is `"warning"`. [extra_attributes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dictionary of attributes to add to every signal, such as the environment or the name of the pipeline. The default is `None`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ImportError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the OTel packages aren't installed. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's validate a small table of orders, which has a missing customer name and two amounts that aren't positive: ::: {#577564de .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl orders = pl.DataFrame( { "order_id": [101, 102, 103, 104, 105], "amount": [29.99, 150.00, -5.00, 75.50, 0.00], "customer": ["Alice", "Bob", None, "Dana", "Eve"], } ) validation = ( pb.Validate(data=orders, tbl_name="orders", thresholds=(0.05, 0.20, 0.40)) .col_vals_not_null(columns="customer") .col_vals_gt(columns="amount", value=0) .interrogate() ) ``` ::: In production, the exporter would use providers that send to a collector. Here, the OTel SDK's `InMemoryMetricReader` keeps the metrics in memory so we can look at them: ::: {#e85aa377 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import InMemoryMetricReader from pointblank.integrations.otel import OTelExporter reader = InMemoryMetricReader() meter_provider = MeterProvider(metric_readers=[reader]) exporter = OTelExporter(meter_provider=meter_provider, extra_attributes={"env": "dev"}) exporter.export(validation) metrics = reader.get_metrics_data().resource_metrics[0].scope_metrics[0].metrics for metric in metrics: for point in metric.data.data_points: value = point.count if hasattr(point, "count") else point.value print(metric.name, value) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` pb.validation.steps.total 2 pb.validation.steps.passed 0 pb.validation.steps.failed 2 pb.validation.test_units.total 10 pb.validation.test_units.passed 7 pb.validation.test_units.failed 3 pb.validation.pass_rate 0.7 pb.validation.duration 0.004554 pb.validation.threshold.warning 2 pb.validation.threshold.error 2 pb.validation.threshold.critical 1 pb.validation.step.duration 1 pb.validation.step.duration 1 ``` ::: ::: Both steps failed, and 7 of the 10 test units passed, for a pass rate of `0.7`. The first step (20% failing) exceeded the warning and error thresholds, and the second (40% failing) exceeded all three. The step duration histogram has a data point for each step, and the value printed for it is its count of one observation. Every data point has the `pb.tbl_name` and `env` attributes (and the histogram's also have the `pb.step.*` ones): ::: {#74416756 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} dict(metrics[0].data.data_points[0].attributes) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'pb.tbl_name': 'orders', 'env': 'dev'} ``` ::: ::: For traces, we give the exporter a `TracerProvider` with an in-memory span exporter. This exporter sends traces only: ::: {#92335070 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter span_exporter = InMemorySpanExporter() tracer_provider = TracerProvider() tracer_provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(span_exporter)) OTelExporter( enable_metrics=False, enable_tracing=True, tracer_provider=tracer_provider ).export(validation) for span in span_exporter.get_finished_spans(): attrs = span.attributes print(span.name, attrs.get("pb.step.assertion_type"), attrs.get("pb.step.n_failed")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` pb.validate.step col_vals_not_null 1 pb.validate.step col_vals_gt 2 pb.validate None None ``` ::: ::: The two `pb.validate.step` spans (one per step, with its number of failing test units) end before the `pb.validate` span that contains them, so they're listed first. The `pb.validate` span has five `threshold_breach` events: two for the first step and three for the second. The [`export()`](`pointblank.integrations.otel.OTelExporter.export`) method has an example of sending log records. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~emit_otel`) : Send the metrics automatically at the end of an interrogation. [](`~FinalActions`) : Run actions after an interrogation. ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [export()](#export){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Send the results of an interrogated validation as OTel signals. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [export()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Send the results of an interrogated validation as OTel signals. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/integrations/otel.py#L241-L364){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature export(validation) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The `export()` method sends the signals that the exporter has enabled (metrics, traces and log records, as described in [`OTelExporter`](`pointblank.integrations.otel.OTelExporter`)) for one interrogated [`Validate`](`pointblank.Validate`) object. The same exporter can export any number of validations, such as one for each table in a pipeline. The counters then add up over the validations, and the `pb.tbl_name` attribute keeps the tables apart. Exporting the same validation twice counts it twice. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [validation]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Validate]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : An interrogated `Validate` object. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The signals are sent to the providers. ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `validation` hasn't been interrogated, or if logging is enabled and there is no `logger_provider=`. In the second case, the metrics and traces have already been sent when the error is raised. [ImportError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the OTel packages aren't installed. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Let's send log records for the steps of a validation that exceeded a threshold. The OTel SDK's `InMemoryLogRecordExporter` keeps the records in memory so we can look at them: ::: {#10282ed7 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl from opentelemetry.sdk._logs import LoggerProvider from opentelemetry.sdk._logs.export import ( InMemoryLogRecordExporter, SimpleLogRecordProcessor, ) from pointblank.integrations.otel import OTelExporter log_exporter = InMemoryLogRecordExporter() logger_provider = LoggerProvider() logger_provider.add_log_record_processor(SimpleLogRecordProcessor(log_exporter)) orders = pl.DataFrame( { "amount": [29.99, 150.00, -5.00, 75.50, 0.00], "customer": ["Alice", "Bob", None, "Dana", "Eve"], } ) validation = ( pb.Validate(data=orders, tbl_name="orders", thresholds=(0.05, 0.20, 0.40)) .col_vals_not_null(columns="customer") .col_vals_gt(columns="amount", value=0) .interrogate() ) exporter = OTelExporter( enable_metrics=False, enable_logging=True, logger_provider=logger_provider ) exporter.export(validation) for log in log_exporter.get_finished_logs(): print(log.log_record.severity_text, log.log_record.body) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ERROR Validation step 1 (col_vals_not_null on 'customer') exceeded error threshold: 20.00% failed CRITICAL Validation step 2 (col_vals_gt on 'amount') exceeded critical threshold: 40.00% failed ``` ::: ::: Each step has one record, at the highest threshold level it exceeded. With `log_level="critical"`, only the second step's record would be sent. A pipeline that checks several tables can use one exporter for all of them. Here, we export a second validation, of a table of customers, with a metrics-only exporter that also gets the first validation: ::: {#866b53df .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import InMemoryMetricReader customers = pl.DataFrame({"customer_id": [1, 2, 3]}) validation_2 = ( pb.Validate(data=customers, tbl_name="customers") .col_vals_not_null(columns="customer_id") .col_vals_gt(columns="customer_id", value=0) .col_vals_lt(columns="customer_id", value=1000) .interrogate() ) reader = InMemoryMetricReader() exporter = OTelExporter(meter_provider=MeterProvider(metric_readers=[reader])) exporter.export(validation) exporter.export(validation_2) metrics = reader.get_metrics_data().resource_metrics[0].scope_metrics[0].metrics steps_total = next(m for m in metrics if m.name == "pb.validation.steps.total") for point in steps_total.data.data_points: print(point.attributes["pb.tbl_name"], point.value) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` orders 2 customers 3 ``` ::: ::: The `pb.validation.steps.total` counter has a data point for each table: 2 steps for `orders` and 3 for `customers`. A dashboard can show them separately, or add them up for a total over the pipeline.
